html:
The Seminole are a Native American people who formed in Spanish Florida in the 1700s. Creek and other Southeastern peoples moved south into lands emptied by the destruction of earlier peoples such as the Apalachee and Timucua, and became a new nation, joined by Africans who had escaped slavery, the Black Seminoles.

The United States fought three Seminole Wars against them between 1817 and 1858, before and after it took Florida from Spain in 1821. Leaders such as Osceola resisted, but under the Indian Removal Act most Seminole were forced west to Indian Territory on the Trail of Tears, where the Seminole Nation of Oklahoma lives today.

A few hundred held out in the Everglades and never signed a peace treaty. Their descendants form the Seminole Tribe of Florida and the Miccosukee Tribe. The Florida tribe opened high-stakes bingo in 1979, starting the era of tribal gaming, and bought the Hard Rock company in 2007. Their roots lie in the Muscogee Creek confederacy.
